question: Is the choice of B0 an artefact of the official score's weight matrix, or does B0 stay the winner under other reasonable rulers?
scope: development folds only, scenario train40, saved predictions only. No holdout labels or scores. No API calls. No model is refit.

candidates.note: B0 appears in every file and must agree row for row; the run asserts that.

metric_variants.form: every variant keeps the chance-corrected shape 1 - sum(W*O)/sum(W*E), so 0 is chance for each
metric_variants.flat_credit: same as official but true-flat rows get (i-j)^2 instead of 0, so correctly answering flat earns credit
metric_variants.linear: W[i,j] = |i-j| * |i-2|^2, so being far wrong costs less steeply
metric_variants.plain_qwk: W[i,j] = (i-j)^2, no extra weight on extreme truth rows
metric_variants.extreme_only: W[i,j] = (i-j)^2 where |i-2| == 2, else 0, so only crash and spike days count

primary_outcome: the rank of B0 among all candidates under each variant
secondary_outcome: where lgb_cost lands, since it is the best forecast by accuracy and direction but the worst under the official score
decision_rule: This is descriptive. Nothing is adopted whatever the result: the holdout was opened on 2026-10-09, B0 won, and the submission is frozen. A variant where B0 loses is reported as a caveat on the conclusion, never as grounds to change the submission.
limitation_stated_in_advance: The non-B0 candidates had their internal knobs (scale, delta, tau, thresholds) chosen under the official score, so this measures how already-frozen predictions rank under a different ruler, not how each model would look if it had been tuned for that ruler.
